newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil judge frees six massacre suspects.
newsitem.headline: Brazil judge frees six massacre suspects.

text.p: A judge has freed six of the 52 police officers accused of killing 21 residents of a Rio de Janeiro shantytown in 1993 after they had spent two years in police custody, a court official said on Wednesday.

She said Rio de Janeiro state judge Jose Geraldo Antonio ordered the release of the six men, who had been confined to police barracks for two years, because of insufficient evidence to prove they were at the scene of the crime. The judge also ordered that 11 other officers be charged in the killings after new evidence emerged, the court official said.

All the police officers stand accused of involvement in the killings on the night of Aug. 30, 1993, when hooded gunmen dressed in black and armed with automatic weapons and shotguns opened fire on Vigario Geral shantytown's residents to avenge the death of four policemen.
The massacre, in which 21 people were killed and four wounded, took place only hours after four military police officers were killed in an ambush by alleged drug traffickers in the shantytown.

The accused face sentences of several hundred years in jail if found guilty on the charges of murder and attempted murder. However, under Brazilian law prisoners serve no more than 30 years, regardless of sentence.

Antonio handed down the first verdict in the massacre case in April, sentencing one officer to 449 years and eight months in jail on 21 charges of murder and four of attempted murder. A new date for continuation of the trial has not been set.
